topics.title: E10 one-off composition guide
topics.text:
# One-off scripts: X01, X09 and X11

Use one-off scripts to compute over selected tools without a conversation moderator. X01's x01-aggregate.chatml exports main input and returns a Task whose value is JSON. Call run_chatml with source, input (an array of report filenames), and tools ["read_file"]. The reader selects the reports root. read_file returns two metadata lines before its file body; the example removes those before JSON parsing. The fixtures retain duplicate failures and exclude passed checks.

Prepare one_off_script before authoring. X09 demonstrates automatic discovery: read the primer's feature overview, then call prepare for the task and follow every next_cursor. A last page with complete=true terminates that query; it is not a complete replacement for earlier pages. After compaction, retrieve missing reference content again. These conventions augment the installed language/runtime reference; they are not audited compiler documentation.

Use let* for dependent tasks and let+ to map the final result. Module calls use parentheses and comma-separated arguments: Task.pure(input), not OCaml's Task.pure input. See chatml.syntax.calls for the exact grammar, chatml.json for JSON constructors, and runtime.invocations.one-off for the execution envelope, limits and selected-tool admission. Direct shell/filesystem access is not part of this script surface.

Validate source through ochat_validate with target one_off_script and the same tools before running it. X11's x11-invalid-call.chatml intentionally uses the invalid application form. Read diagnostic topic_ids, retrieve those topics for this task, repair, and validate again. Missing record fields and a Task returning an ordinary record instead of JSON are other useful failures (chatml.types and runtime.invocations.one-off). Validation is non-executing and its identity grants no execution authority.

Run only against approved example data. A later read outside reports remains denied even after successful validation. The source bundle's tests execute this aggregation through the real script/tool boundary with offline providers; they do not prove model authoring quality.
